meta.tag: 3 agent worker processes (thread executor, MAX_SESSIONS 40 each), stub STT, mock LLM, local Piper TTS; LiveKit 1.13.10
meta.note: **Result: 100 sessions per node was NOT reached on this machine.** The three worker processes plateau at about 4.7 CPU cores (≈ 1.5 cores per Python process: the GIL bounds one process) and voice-to-voice stays under ~0.9 s up to 20 sessions (p95 1.29 s at 30); at 40 sessions replies stop arriving (overload, no reply measured). So one worker process handles roughly 10-12 calls; 100+ sessions per node means ~9 worker processes on ≥ 16 cores, which is what the Helm defaults assume (`maxSessions: 12`) but which was not demonstrated here. The generator, the SFU and Docker share the same 10-core laptop VM, so absolute numbers are pessimistic; STT/LLM network latency and rate limits are excluded by design. The 'dropped frames' and 'NS+VAD' columns are empty because the Prometheus query returned no data during this run. Before the thread-mode fixes in this phase (shutdown hangs, polling playout) leaked sessions kept burning CPU after calls ended.
